relevant_files.role: LanguageInfo struct definition and get_language_info/get_ts_language match arms

conventions.testing: Unit tests in same file with #[cfg(test)] mod tests; integration tests via SemanticExtractor
conventions.linting: clippy with deny for undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used; warn for must_use_candidate, redundant_clone, needless_pass_by_value, large_enum_variant
conventions.error_handling: Option<T> returns, expect/unwrap for static patterns, Result propagation in parsers

patterns: Language registration pattern: mod declaration, EXTENSION_MAP entry, get_language_info/get_ts_language match arms
Query constants: ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY
Handler functions: extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance
constraints: DEFUSE_QUERY is mandatory (LanguageInfo.defuse_query is Option<&'static str> and every language sets it)
No feature flags for language dependencies (unconditional compilation)
Model after java.rs for handler patterns
test_coverage: Java has comprehensive unit tests for extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance, element_query happy path, and defuse_query write site. Swift should follow similar pattern.

library_findings.notes: Dependency is tree-sitter-language ^0.1.0 only; tree-sitter is dev-only, no version conflict with workspace tree-sitter = 0.26.13
Workspace dependency used by all language crates

approaches.name: Full Java-style integration
approaches.description: Create swift.rs with all query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY) and handlers (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance). Wire up in mod.rs and lang.rs.
pros: All handlers available for advanced analysis
cons: More code to write and test
Some handlers may not be needed for Swift

approaches.name: Minimal integration with required DEFUSE_QUERY
approaches.description: Create swift.rs with only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, and DEFUSE_QUERY. Set extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, find_method_for_receiver, extract_inheritance to None. Wire up in mod.rs and lang.rs.
pros: Less code to write and test
DEFUSE_QUERY is the only required handler per issue
cons: May need to add handlers later

approaches.name: Minimal with extract_inheritance
approaches.description: Create swift.rs with all queries plus extract_inheritance handler (required for inheritance analysis). Set other handlers to None. Wire up in mod.rs and lang.rs.

recommendation: Approach 3 (Minimal with extract_inheritance) - The issue explicitly mentions extract_inheritance as a reference handler to model after java.rs, and inheritance analysis is a key feature. DEFUSE_QUERY is mandatory per the issue. Other handlers can be added later if needed.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
inheritance_walk_citation: From tree-sitter-swift grammar (alex-pinkus/tree-sitter-swift): Walk class_declaration node's _inheritance_specifiers child. For each inheritance_specifier, read the inherits_from field which points to a user_type node. Extract the type_identifier text from user_type to get the base type name. Multiple inheritance_specifiers are siblings (comma-separated in source).
